items.title: Op ed: Beyond the Battlefield: How strategic centralization deepens Somalia’s political, security crisis
items.description: Somalia’s worsening security crisis is increasingly rooted in political fragmentation, contested federal authority, and declining public trust, rather than military weakness alone, writes Adam Daud Ahmed. He argues that disputes between Mogadishu and regional administrations, coupled with the government’s failure to sustain liberated communities, are creating opportunities for Al Shabaab to regain influence. The author notes, "Somalia risks continuing to win battles while losing the political foundations necessary to win the war."
